# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-246-248 (§§246–248)

Reviewer pass 1. Files read: conventions.md, runbook.md, run3/RUNBOOK.md §2, packet.md, units.json, novel-forms.json, known-forms.json, secret-history-glossary.json, the published parts (all `secret-history-*.json`, in particular 01-06 and 245-245). Only `units.json` (edited in place by script) and this file were touched. No build was run; no gloss.json was created.

Checks that passed with no change: all 58 units have `t`, `l`, `i`, `n`; `t` equals the packet words (U56 is the one word printed as two, `Waṅgiṅ Čiṅsaṅ`, counted as one); the 445 words are consumed exactly once; `ln` is right in every unit and `p: true` falls on the first unit of each § (U0, U16, U35); no unit crosses a §; every word has a morph and every morph a gloss; the Ming bracket in each first morph equals the packet's Ming gloss (Güṅžü has none in the source); quote marks match Shiratori's (after the two fixes below); house names (Jebe, Chinggis Qahan, Münlig, Qongqotan, Altan Qan, Qara-Kitad, Teb-Tenggeri, Quchar, Jamuqa) agree with the published parts.

## Findings refused or left (with reason)
- U1 `i` "at dawn" for šira-da (yellow): the note already says the guess is doubtful; `l` keeps "yellow-at". Left.
- U2 `i` "confirmed of Teb there": awkward but the note states the grammar is uncertain; no better reading from the Ming. Left.
- U4 `i` "set my hand and foot upon my younger brothers": note gives both readings and admits doubt. Left.
- U9 `i` "as Jamuqa, Altan, Quchar and the others were": a reading of the genitive Qučar-tan-u; the note says what became of them is not supplied. Left.
- U14/deṅgečekün: the stem deṅgeče- is kept (the glossary has only the adjective deṅgečen); gloss says "inferred". The glosser should add it.
- U16 `i` "Kitad people" (Ming 金國): the note explains the Ming; house practice keeps Kitad. Left.
- U17 hünegen as "fox"/"Fox Pass": note flags it may be a taken-over name. Left.
- U27 baitala as bai- + -tala: the glossary's entry offers this as its second reading; Ming 堆般 fits it. Left.
- U39 `i` rearranges the genitives into apposition ("our leading troops, the brave and bold Qara-Kitad …"); sense is the same as U26's rendering and the note says so. Left.
- U47 `i` "the Qan" for Qān-a: the note names the Mongol Qan as receiver. Left.
- U50 `i` keeps Shiratori's marks; correct.

New or changed lemmas against the glossary: qoton (add "walled town, city"), daγa- (add "to bear, endure"), balaγad (singular balaγasun now occurs), else-, ič-/ičuγa-, erke + -d, aisu-, bol- + -γa-, žaγ̇ur-a, kürge-, ködöl- + -ge-, Žürčed, heġüšije-, žöbšije-, dülilige-, daruča-.
